# Complete benchmark results

This page shows every scenario in the comparative Go benchmark and
process-memory suite, not a selected subset. Each implementation receives the
same deterministic inputs, and the
suite proves semantic equivalence before it records timings. Results are the
median of 10 repetitions with `-benchmem`, summarized by the repository's
pinned `benchstat`.

**How to read the advantage columns:** 🟢 positive means this pure-Go library
is better; 🔴 negative means the official cgo binding is better; ⚪ marks equal
or statistically indistinguishable results. The faster or smaller value is
**bold**. Time advantage is `(uber / this library − 1) × 100`; `benchstat`
determines time ties at p≥0.05.

> Results are machine- and compiler-specific. Compare implementations within
> one environment only; never compare absolute Darwin values with Linux values.

- [Apple M1 Max · darwin/arm64](#apple-m1-max--darwinarm64)
- [GitHub Actions AMD EPYC 7763 · linux/amd64](#github-actions-amd-epyc-7763--linuxamd64)

## Apple M1 Max · `darwin/arm64`

go version go1.26.5 darwin/arm64; `Apple M1 Max`; clang — Apple clang version 21.0.0 (clang-2100.1.1.101). Across all scenarios: **this library 12 wins**, **uber/h3-go 20 wins**, 1 no clear difference.

### Process-level memory

Go and C memory; retained Go heap is sampled after forced garbage collection.

### Process-level memory

## Measurement caveats

Go's `B/op` and `allocs/op` measure Go-heap activity only. They do not see
allocations made inside the binding's C code. The process-level memory matrices
linked above capture whole-process RSS and retained-heap behavior and should be
used alongside the Go allocation tables. Linux measurements come from a shared
GitHub Actions runner, so small deltas are especially susceptible to noise. See
the [methodology and reproduction guide](README.md) for the full protocol.
